question.text: The governing law clause in the PPM of Zuari Tech AIF states that the fund documentation shall be governed by the laws of India with courts in Mumbai having exclusive jurisdiction. What does 'exclusive jurisdiction' mean?

answer.text: Only the Supreme Court of India can hear disputes related to the fund
The fund can only invest in companies headquartered in Mumbai
Any dispute that goes to litigation (as opposed to arbitration) can only be filed in courts located in Mumbai, excluding all other courts
Only investors residing in Mumbai can invest in the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: An exclusive jurisdiction clause is a standard contractual forum-selection provision. It states that if a dispute proceeds to litigation (rather than arbitration), it can be filed only in the named city's courts (Mumbai here), and all other courts are excluded. It does not concern where the fund may invest, who may invest in the fund, or whether disputes must go to the Supreme Court (which is principally an appellate forum, not a court of first instance for commercial contracts). The Trap: The Supreme Court option confuses exclusive jurisdiction (a specific city's lower courts) with appellate jurisdiction. The "Mumbai-headquartered companies only" and "Mumbai-resident investors only" options confuse a forum-selection clause with substantive investment or eligibility restrictions. Note: The specific contractual meaning of an exclusive jurisdiction / Mumbai-forum clause is not explicitly explained in the cited workbook chapter (Series XIX-A_AIF (Category I and II) Distributors_Dec-version PDF.pdf, pp. 85, 94, 191). The framing above is general legal/industry knowledge about forum-selection clauses in fund documentation.
